Summary: Control the path from scope freeze to cutover, live watch, rollback readiness, and learning with explicit release evidence, approvals, and watch ownership.
ValueStatement: Lower release risk by turning scattered evidence, deployment choreography, and go-live authority into one typed control process that works for human teams and AI-assisted orchestration.
InterfaceContractSummary: Implementation outputs, quality evidence, operational readiness, support coverage, and release-window constraints are merged into one bounded deployment decision.
GovernanceNotes: A release is not ready because a team feels ready; it is ready only when the control process can prove scope, evidence, approval, and rollback preparedness.
ChangeSummary: Built from SSDF verification/release evidence, SAMM governance maturity, and operational cutover discipline suitable for shared-responsibility SaaS delivery.
GovernancePolicySummary: Go-live requires scope freeze, evidence synthesis, change-window coverage, rollback readiness, explicit approval, and named watch coverage.
ConstitutionRuleSummary: No one may reinterpret an approval outside the conditions that were explicitly recorded.
OperatingModeSummary: Guarded live execution: automation may prepare, validate, and monitor, but final approval and exception handling remain human.
SimulationReadinessSummary: Supports cutover rehearsal, watch roster simulation, dashboard integration, and post-release control tuning.
Metrics: Number of open exceptions at go/no-go
Risks: Deployment scope drifts after evidence collection.
Watch coverage or escalation ownership is incomplete.
Rollback plan exists on paper but is not operationally ready.
Approval is issued without clear live conditions.
TailoringRules: For low-risk internal releases, merge evidence review and change-window check if watch coverage remains typed.
For customer-visible releases, customer communication artifacts should be linked even if not locally stored in the template.
For AI-generated release notes or deployment plans, require prompt-package and review evidence artifacts.

Steps.Title: Freeze release scope and deployment boundary
Steps.Subtitle: Make the release target explicit
Steps.Notes: Capture the exact change set, environment boundary, rollout strategy, and excluded items before readiness claims start.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Candidate release contents, change logs, linked work items, and deployment boundary.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Frozen release scope with explicit inclusions and exclusions.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Scope freeze note and environment targeting summary.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Change manager controls the frozen boundary; delivery manager reviews business commitment impact.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: No readiness claim is valid if scope can still silently drift.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Change manager owns boundary discipline.
Delivery manager reviews plan impact.
Operational boundary review remains explicit.

Steps.Title: Synthesize readiness evidence and open risks
Steps.Subtitle: Gather all proof into one release lens
Steps.Notes: Combine implementation state, QA proof, security findings, operational checks, and known open items into one decision-ready package.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Frozen release scope, QA runs, security notes, environment status, and known exceptions.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Release readiness package with explicit open-risk inventory.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Release readiness report and linked evidence references.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Delivery manager and QA lead own evidence synthesis; security reviewer and service owner contribute risk posture.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not summarize evidence that you have not actually inspected or linked.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Delivery manager remains accountable for the integrated view.
QA review confirms objective proof coverage.
Security review remains explicit.
Service owner reviews operational readiness.

Steps.Title: Rehearse cutover and confirm watch coverage
Steps.Subtitle: Operational readiness is rehearsed, not assumed
Steps.Notes: Exercise the cutover sequence, support handoffs, and watch roster so operators know exactly who acts on which signal during the real release.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Release readiness package, deployment sequence, monitoring plan, and on-call availability.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Rehearsed cutover package and watch roster with gaps called out.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Watch roster, cutover rehearsal notes, and gap log.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Change manager owns choreography; platform engineer and service owner validate live-operability.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: If critical watch roles are missing or unreachable, hold the release.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Cutover choreography remains with the change manager.
Platform engineer reviews operational feasibility.
Service owner validates coverage and escalation.
Approver may observe rehearsal for high-risk releases.

Steps.Title: Run final security review and go/no-go approval
Steps.Subtitle: The last gate decides under explicit conditions
Steps.Notes: Combine the readiness package, cutover rehearsal, rollback proof, and open exceptions into the final release decision.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Readiness package, rehearsal output, rollback plan, and any exception requests.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Approved or held release decision with explicit conditions.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Release approval record and exception note if applicable.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Release approver owns the final decision; security reviewer may hold the release for unresolved control gaps.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: No release may proceed on informal approval; block when artifact recovery is required for missing or invalid go/no-go evidence.

BranchOutcomes.Title: Go
BranchOutcomes.Description: Release is approved under the recorded conditions.

BranchOutcomes.Title: Hold
BranchOutcomes.Description: Release is held pending gap closure or explicit exception resolution.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Final go/no-go authority remains with the release approver.
Security review remains explicit.
Operational risk owner reviews live conditions.

Steps.Title: Execute cutover and observe live telemetry
Steps.Subtitle: Run only inside the approved envelope
Steps.Notes: Execute the approved deployment sequence, monitor live indicators, and invoke rollback if the approved threshold is breached.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Go decision, cutover brief, watch roster, telemetry thresholds, and rollback triggers.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Executed release with live status and next action record.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Operator execution note, telemetry snapshots, and rollback note if used.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Platform engineer performs the cutover; change manager controls timing and handoffs.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Rollback immediately when thresholds or instructions dictate it.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Execution remains with the platform engineer.
Change manager reviews cutover timing.
Service owner remains fallback during live watch.

Steps.Title: Confirm stability, close watch, and capture learning
Steps.Subtitle: A release ends only after stability is explicit
Steps.Notes: Confirm whether the service is stable, close the live watch, and record improvements for the next release.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Cutover outcome, telemetry trend, incident or support notes, and watch coverage observations.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Closed release watch with stability declaration and improvements.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Service owner declares stability; change manager closes the change record; delivery manager captures learning.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not declare stability without observed evidence for the agreed horizon.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Stability declaration remains with service owner.
Change manager closes control records.
Delivery manager captures follow-up work.

Steps.Title: Hold the release and track gap closure
Steps.Subtitle: A held release still needs a typed end state
Steps.Notes: Record the hold decision, missing controls, and required gap-closure plan so the release can resume from an explicit governance checkpoint instead of an informal retry.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Held release decision with unresolved gaps or exception requests.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Closed release attempt with explicit hold conditions and reopening trigger.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Release hold note and gap-closure summary.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Release approver and change manager define the hold boundary and required next checkpoint.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not reopen the release path until the recorded hold conditions are satisfied explicitly.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Release approver owns the held decision.
Change manager preserves the reopening conditions.

LocalRoles.Summary: Change-window and stakeholder-readiness owner for production deployment events.
LocalRoles.Purpose: Coordinate production change timing, communications, operational readiness, and deployment-event discipline.
LocalRoles.StaffingIntent: A release/change specialist responsible for controlled execution during go-live windows.
LocalRoles.SnapshotSummary: Change-window and stakeholder-readiness owner for production deployment events.
LocalRoles.SeniorityBand: Senior change or release operations management
KnowledgeRequirements: Knowledge of change windows, deployment communications, stakeholder notifications, and cutover discipline.
Ability to coordinate activities across release, support, infrastructure, and customer-facing teams.
Understanding of operational readiness checks and fallback ownership during go-live.
Ability to recognize when an apparently ready release lacks event-level discipline.
Knowledge of maintenance-window governance and approval paths.
Ability to document go-live conditions, hold points, and rollback triggers cleanly.
ExperienceRequirements: Has run or coordinated production change events with multiple parties involved.
Has handled go/no-go checkpoints and late-breaking blockers.
Has executed communication and support readiness for customer-impacting releases.
Has worked with release approvers and operators during deployment windows.
Has captured lessons after difficult cutovers or rollback events.
DecisionRights: Approve change-event readiness from a coordination perspective.
Stop the event when required stakeholders or communications are missing.
Own the authoritative event plan and hold points.
CollaborationExpectations: Coordinate with release approver, platform engineer, and service owner.
Keep deployment-event timing and contact points unambiguous.
Ensure customer-facing teams know what to expect.
Record deviations and lessons for future release playbooks.
AntiPatterns: Assuming technical readiness automatically implies event readiness.
Running change windows without contact, escalation, or support clarity.
Failing to preserve a clean go-live timeline.
FitnessEvidence: Event plans that enabled controlled go-live execution.
Documented hold points and escalation paths actually used during releases.
Stakeholder feedback that deployment coordination was clear.
Improvement of cutover discipline over time.

LocalArtifacts.Summary: Named on-watch roster for the first live risk window during deployment or cutover.
LocalArtifacts.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for the specific deployment event and later incident or retrospective review.
LocalArtifacts.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must include actual names, contact paths, and timing, not placeholder roles only.

LocalChecklists.Summary: Checks whether the cutover or deployment path was rehearsed enough to trust the event plan.
LocalChecklists.EntryCriteria: A significant release or cutover event is nearing execution.
LocalChecklists.ExitCriteria: Rehearsal or dry-run evidence is sufficient for the declared risk level.
Checks: Cutover sequence has been walked through or rehearsed.
Hold points and rollback triggers are understood.
Support and communication escalation paths are tested.

LocalValidations.Summary: Confirms the first live risk window has real staffed monitoring and decision coverage.
LocalValidations.PassCriteria: Named watchers, approvers, and escalation paths cover the critical deployment horizon.
LocalValidations.FailCriteria: Deployment depends on unstated availability or placeholder coverage.
LocalValidations.EscalationRule: Escalate to release approver and service owner before go-live.

LocalPrompts.Summary: Prompt scaffold for cutover command briefs at go-live checkpoints.
RefusalConditions: Refuse to summarize the cutover as green if watch coverage or trigger logic is missing.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Coordinate production change timing, communications, operational readiness, and deployment-event discipline.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: A release/change specialist responsible for controlled execution during go-live windows.
RoleUsages.Notes: Change-window and stakeholder-readiness owner for production deployment events.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Keep the process executable by turning desired outcomes into a feasible, staffed, time-aware delivery path with explicit escalation triggers.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: A senior delivery-side coordinator with enough authority to challenge unrealistic dates, surface hidden dependencies, and keep multiple roles synchronized.
RoleUsages.Notes: Flow owner for sequencing, staffing realism, dependency control, and execution escalation.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Represent live-service constraints, operational history, and post-release accountability in change decisions.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: A domain-aligned owner with authority over service-level objectives, support load, and operational trade-offs.
RoleUsages.Notes: Operational accountability owner for a live service, product surface, or bounded business capability.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Challenge whether the delivered change is proven enough for its risk profile and make test evidence decision-ready for release governance.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: A senior test leader able to shape strategy, select evidence depth, and identify where automation is not enough.
RoleUsages.Notes: Quality owner for coverage depth, evidence quality, and release confidence.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Ensure changes touching trust boundaries, sensitive data, dependencies, or operational attack surface are reviewed proportionally and documented defensibly.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: A senior security practitioner who can translate security risk into concrete engineering and governance decisions.
RoleUsages.Notes: Security gate owner for threat assessment, exception handling, and trust-boundary decisions.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Provide the reliable platform path required to build, deploy, observe, and if necessary roll back changes safely.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: A technical specialist in CI/CD, environments, infrastructure, and observability integration.
RoleUsages.Notes: Environment and delivery-pipeline owner for build integrity, deployment mechanics, and operational guardrails.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Decide whether the accumulated evidence is sufficient to expose the change to real users, data, and operational load.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: A senior operational or governance authority who can accept release risk on behalf of the organization.
RoleUsages.Notes: Final go-live decision owner for production promotion and rollback preparedness.
